newsitem.title: CANADA: Aircraft passenger fatalities jump in 1996 - ICAO.
newsitem.headline: Aircraft passenger fatalities jump in 1996 - ICAO.

text.p: The number of aircraft passenger deaths reported by the world's scheduled air carriers jumped to 1,135 in 1996 from 710 in 1995, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) said on Monday.

Passenger fatalities per 100 million passenger-kilometres also rose, to 0.05 in 1996 from 0.03 in 1995. The scheduled air carriers of ICAO's 185 contracting states reported 23 aircraft accidents involving passenger fatalities in 1996, compared with 26 in 1995.
For non-scheduled air services, there were 25 fatal accidents in 1996, down from 40 in 1995, accounting for 479 passenger fatalities versus 391.

ICAO said 14 incidents of unlawful interference were reported ub 1996, in which 126 people were killed and 53 injured. In 1995, there were 13 such incidents in which two people were killed and one perpetrator was injured.
ICAO is an agency of the United Nations created in 1944 to promote civil aviation safety and development.
